content.title: 2027 Social Security COLA Forecast: A Disappointing 2.8% Increase Projected
content.text: April 12, 2026 at 5:50 AM GMT+0 Early projections for the Social Security cost-of-living adjustment indicate a potentially disappointing outcome for the upcoming year. According to a report from Yahoo Finance, the Senior Citizens League, a senior advocacy group, is forecasting a 2.8% COLA for 2027 based on current inflation data.Projected COLA mirrors current yearThis preliminary figure would result in a benefits increase identical to the adjustment retirees received in the current year. Official determination of the annual raise, which is calculated using third-quarter inflation data, remains several months away.Why a 2.8% increase presents challengesAnalysts describe this projection as a worst-case scenario for many beneficiaries. A 2.8% inflation rate is considered high relative to the Federal Reserve's target, potentially eroding the purchasing power of retirees who often hold conservative investments. Furthermore, after experiencing larger post-pandemic adjustments, the prospect of another modest increase may disappoint those facing rising Medicare costs.The final COLA calculation could change if inflation patterns shift before the official measurement period. Slower price growth would improve retirees' financial position, while accelerating inflation, though harmful to budgets, could lead to a larger subsequent benefits increase. 1.
